tagline: Consoles, mobile hits, esports and the biggest entertainment industry on earth.
why: Gaming is bigger than film and music combined, and it's no longer just teenagers: most adults play something, from mobile games on the MTR to big console releases. Gamers talk about new launches, favourite franchises, platforms and the industry's drama. Knowing the key consoles, games and terms lets you connect with the many people who play.

essentials.title: Platforms
essentials.body: PlayStation 5 (Sony), Xbox Series X|S (Microsoft), Nintendo Switch 2 (launched June 2025), PC (mostly through Steam), and mobile, the biggest by revenue.

essentials.title: Genres
essentials.body: Shooters (Call of Duty), RPGs (Final Fantasy, Elden Ring), sports (EA FC), battle royale (Fortnite), open world (Zelda, GTA), strategy, puzzle and more.

essentials.title: Free-to-play and gacha
essentials.body: Many games are free but make money from in-game purchases. Gacha games like Genshin Impact sell randomised characters.

essentials.title: Live service
essentials.body: Games updated for years with new content, like Fortnite or Destiny, rather than one-off releases.

essentials.title: Esports and streaming
essentials.body: Competitive gaming (League of Legends, Valorant, Dota 2) fills arenas, and streamers on Twitch and YouTube are celebrities.

essentials.title: China and Asia matter
essentials.body: Chinese companies like Tencent and miHoYo are giants, and Black Myth: Wukong (2024) showed China can make AAA console games.

timeline.event: Super Mario Bros. on the NES.
World of Warcraft makes online gaming mainstream.
Pokémon Go sends people into the streets.
Nintendo Switch and Fortnite Battle Royale.
PS5, Xbox Series X and Genshin Impact launch; pandemic gaming boom.
Elden Ring becomes a global hit.
Black Myth: Wukong sells tens of millions of copies.
Switch 2 launches; Hollow Knight: Silksong finally releases; GTA VI delayed again.

now.headline: GTA VI out on Thursday
now.detail: After two delays, Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November on PlayStation and Xbox; reviews reportedly drop the day before.

now.headline: A box with no disc
now.detail: Retail boxes went on sale on 12 November with just a download code inside, and the install is about 230GB.

now.headline: US$1 billion before launch
now.detail: Sensor Tower estimates over 10 million pre-orders and about US$1 billion in sales; three in four are on PlayStation.

now.headline: Record watch
now.detail: GTA VI is expected to beat GTA V's record of US$815.7 million in its first 24 hours.

now.headline: Game Awards nominees on 17 November
now.detail: The show is 10 December; GTA VI and the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake (96 on Metacritic) are eligible.

local.headline: Mobile on the MTR
local.detail: Mobile gaming is everywhere on commutes; gacha games are hugely popular.

local.headline: Sham Shui Po and Mong Kok
local.detail: Game shops sell consoles and Japanese imports.

local.headline: Arcades
local.detail: Hong Kong's game centres have shrunk, but some nostalgic arcades survive.

local.headline: Esports venues
local.detail: Esports cafés and events have grown, with support from Cyberport.
